title: EuroHPC AI Factories: free supercomputing access for EU AI startups – calls open
content:
AI Factories aim to offer advanced computing resources and expert support to European industry and scientific communities.
These facilities will enable the development of large-scale AI models, foster the adoption of AI technologies across the EU, and contribute to building skills and expertise in the field of artificial intelligence.
Different access modes and types are available to meet the needs of users with different levels of requirements and expertise.
AI for Industrial Innovation
The AI Factories Industrial Innovation track includes three access mode, targeting different use cases and compute needs.
- Playground access, providing limited resources for entry-level users
- Fast Lane access, for users already familiar with HPC requiring up to 50,000 GPU hours
- Large Scale access, catering to AI models and applications requiring more than 50,000 GPU hours
The Industrial Innovation Access modes are open and free-of-charge to AI SMEs (including startups) for innovation purposes. Other industrial applications can benefit from pay-per-use commercial access.
AI for Science and Collaborative projects
The AI for Science and Collaborative EU projects access mode will support AI applications for science, with a focus on ethical Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and cutting-edge foundation Models and Generative AI, including Large Language Models. This mode is intended for scientific research activities that rely on AI models as part of their research workflow.
This access mode is open and free of charge to eligible public and private users, primarily for publicly funded research, as well as for industrial applications in collaborative projects which are funded by Horizon Europe or the Digital Europe Programme

report.summary: EuroHPC AI Factories are opening free supercomputing access modes for EU AI startups, researchers, and collaborative projects to build and scale AI models.
report.background: Europe has been racing to strengthen its AI compute base as training large models requires scarce, expensive GPUs. EuroHPC JU pools EU and national supercomputing resources, and its AI Factories initiative links those systems with AI-optimized services and expert support. The program is meant to help startups, SMEs, and scientists who cannot easily buy hyperscale compute, while advancing EU goals on sovereign AI, industrial adoption, and skills. The access modes reflect different user maturity: entry-level playgrounds, fast lanes for HPC-experienced teams, and large-scale allocations for frontier workloads. Science and collaborative tracks target publicly funded research and Horizon Europe or Digital Europe projects, including ethical AI, machine learning, foundation models, and generative AI. The latest calls make clear that eligible AI SMEs and startups can use the industrial innovation track free of charge, while other industrial users can pay for commercial access.
key_points: Industrial Innovation offers three doors: Playground provides limited resources for newcomers; Fast Lane gives up to 50,000 GPU hours to teams familiar with HPC; Large Scale covers projects needing more than 50,000 GPU hours, such as large model training or heavy inference.

The Industrial Innovation track is free for AI SMEs and startups using it for innovation. Other industrial applications can use pay-per-use commercial access. This separates public support for small AI innovators from commercial consumption by larger or non-eligible firms.

A separate AI for Science and Collaborative EU Projects mode supports ethical AI, machine learning, foundation models, generative AI and LLMs in research workflows. It is free for eligible public and private users, mainly publicly funded research and Horizon Europe or Digital Europe collaborative projects.

AI Factories are not just GPU allocations. They combine advanced computing with expert support and aim to help develop large-scale models, spread AI adoption across the EU, and build AI/HPC skills. Users should expect application review, eligibility checks and allocation constraints.
report.impact: For the AI industry, free and subsidized access lowers the cost of experimenting with and training large models, giving EU startups a chance to compete without immediately relying on commercial clouds. It could strengthen Europe’s sovereign AI stack and attract investment to local AI factories. For developers, the opportunity is real GPU time plus HPC expertise, but they must adapt to batch scheduling, containers, distributed training and proposal-based allocation. Regular users may eventually see more EU-built models and AI services, especially in science and local languages, but access is not universal: eligibility, capacity and project review will limit who benefits. The program is a strategic compute subsidy rather than open-ended free cloud.
report.tools: Start with the EuroHPC JU AI Factories access page and national AI Factory contact points. Existing EuroHPC systems such as LUMI, Leonardo, MeluXina and JUWELS host relevant capacity. For preparation, learn the common open-source HPC/AI stack: Slurm for scheduling, Apptainer/Singularity for containers, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, DeepSpeed or Megatron-LM for distributed training, and Ray for scaling.
